description:
Several AVX2 kernel wrappers in `gf2-kernels-simd` call `unsafe` functions without a stated safety contract; every unsafe boundary in the kernel crate carries one.

## Background

`crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/avx2.rs` exposes safe wrapper functions that call `#[target_feature]` kernels inside `unsafe` blocks. The fused AND-popcount route and its carry-save sibling state their contract with a `# Safety` rustdoc section on the kernel and a `// SAFETY:` comment at the call. The population-count, complement, find-first, shift and M4RM wrappers of the same module call their kernels without a `// SAFETY:` comment, and most `unsafe fn` items there have no `# Safety` section. The repository isolates production `unsafe` to the kernel crates on the condition that every unsafe boundary has an explicit safety contract.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every `unsafe fn` in `crates/gf2-kernels-simd` has a `# Safety` rustdoc section covering pointer validity, slice lengths, aliasing and required target features.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every `unsafe` block in the crate has a `// SAFETY:` comment naming the runtime gate or invariant that discharges the callee's contract.
- [hard] REQ-03: The instruction text of every affected symbol is unchanged, shown by a committed comparison of the regenerated assembly listings, and the shared behavioural suites pass with and without the `simd` feature on Rust 1.95.

## Notes

Found while verifying the dense-parity no-adoption outcome, which closed the gap for the fused AND-popcount route only. Comments and rustdoc carry the contract in the shortest form that states it.
title: State the safety contract at every AVX2 kernel unsafe boundary
